findings.claim: OrchestraBench: keyword/flag router 0% vs intent-reasoning router 100% on adversarial cases; recovery tiers tool faults 1.0, ambiguous delegation 0.30, latent/semantic 0.0; cascade radius 0.9 to 4.7 over depth 3-7; blind retry reproduces latent faults.

Source record maps OCR weak cells to the older 18-lang probe: Santali 53.91, Kashmiri 54.82, OldScan 55.3, Odia 80.01 (CER-like scores in the 18x100 lock); argues intent-reasoning routing for ambiguous script delegation.

AdaptOrch: orchestration topology dominates model capability when LLMs converge; 4 topologies (parallel, sequential, hierarchical, hybrid); routing O(|V|+|E|); 12-23% over static single-topology baselines on SWE-bench/GPQA/RAG (not OCR).

Adversarial Review (3 agents: coder, reviewer, critic) tops LiveCodeBench vs a 5-agent baseline; naive AR shows false-consensus failure; explicit disagreement constraints fix it. Insight: shape of disagreement matters more than agent count.
Campaign operating model (locked per 'campaign law'): 3-agent Engine/Verdict/Miss; Verdict specifies fixes, Miss applies, Verdict re-verifies; fix-loop max 2 rounds; human validation call at H44-48.
Anthropic Managed Agents: stateless harness + durable session log + containers as cattle; p50 TTFT -~60%, p95 >90%. Mapped to unified-memory vault + isolated worktrees for crash recovery.
Anthropic multi-agent research: Opus lead + Sonnet subagents beat single Opus by 90.2%; agents ~4x tokens vs chat, multi-agent ~15x. Early errors: 50 subagents for simple queries.
Anthropic 5 coordination patterns: generator-verifier, parallel teammates, orchestrator-workers, message bus, shared state; subagents sequential unless explicitly parallelized.

Multi-agent only justified when context exceeded, distinct skills, or parallelizable work; teams often find better single-agent prompting equals elaborate systems. Relevant caution for a small ~2-expert OCR plan.

Agent Capsules: against LangGraph 14-agent pipeline 51% fewer fine-mode tokens, 42% fewer compound tokens at +0.020/+0.017 quality; vs DSPy 5-agent 19% fewer at parity, 68% fewer than MIPROv2 at +0.052. Source maps to 18x100=1800 calls.

Self-Evaluation Bias (arXiv 2607.25152): agent self-grading 'progress mirage': 54 cycles, claimed improvement every cycle, 56% had measured delta<=0; self-verdict gate eroded best state 19%; strong in-band judge accepted 44% regressions, rejected 38% improvements; vanished with artifact-verifiable success.
Implication for plan: gates must be out-of-band artifact-verifiable (hash leak gate HW0, held-out writers), not LLM self-judgement; Engine cannot self-verify.

Framework selection recorded: LangGraph chosen over CrewAI/AutoGen for deterministic offline pipeline; CrewAI DIES (memory embedder needs training data, blocked until W6 freeze); OpenAI Agents SDK needs paid keys but pattern transfers (Agents-as-Tools).
Pipeline design recorded: code-driven main pipeline (PPT_SPEC fixed DAG) with LLM-driven per-language engine selection only inside Engine; 'God Agent' (single agent for all langs) rejected.
Council-multi-model external critique (Codex/OpenAI) DIES: no paid keys; honest-empty (mark review absent) is correct; no local alternative specified.
Probe22 execution law: sec 6.4 GT verdicts LOCKED, sec 10 closed; RFC pipeline must respect locked verdicts; engine configs fixed per language.

Loop-design-check: 5 failure modes (spinning, Goodhart-gaming verifier, wrong answer to completion, decidability etc.); machine-decidable goal = CER per language; judge independence; human red-line at validation call.

Gate timeline recorded: Gate 1 = validation call H44-48 (W6 training go/no-go decided AT the call); Gate 2 = W6 freeze after Wed 2026-10-01; campaign end ~04:23 IST Tue Sep 29; 'no training until W6 freeze' constraint.

findings.claim: Evidence law sec 9: every record tagged PRIMARY/MEASURED/DERIVED/CONTRADICTION/UNKNOWN/REJECTED/DEAD and names decision it can change; honest-empty (unified-memory stores only measured evidence); 18x100 = 1800 evidence records.
Parallel lanes A (Engine 18 langs), B (Verdict), C (Miss+monitoring), up to 3x18=54 parallel agents with isolated worktrees.
Formal-verification agent papers (2511.17330, VMAO 2603.11445) rejected for OCR: quality is empirical CER, not provable; verification-driven iterative loop pattern retained.
AOrchestra dynamic sub-agent creation REJECTED: fixed per-language engine configs preferred (probe22 locked verdicts).
SPOQ prompt self-optimization treated as training-adjacent: prompt fixes applied by Miss, max 2 iterations, not Engine self-optimization.
Long-context benchmarks (Oolong 2511.02817, LongBench Pro 2601.02872) DEAD for OCR: per-sample independent, no aggregation.

GAN-style continuous iteration rejected: campaign has fix-loop max 2 and is time-bounded (~04:23 Sep 29), not quality-bounded. Prime Agent self-improving harness: patterns survive, self-improvement blocked until W6.
Synchronous Engine->Verdict->Miss chosen for determinism; async rejected (coordination complexity), though Anthropic notes sync bottleneck.
Eval thresholds stated for weak cells: Santali >55, Kashmiri >55, OldScan >55, Odia >80 (CER-per-language scorer; per Anthropic 'Demystifying evals': task+scorer+threshold).
Infrastructure noise quantification: controlled environments, repeated runs; Probe22 18x100 lock = controlled baseline; honest-empty for unknown noise.
Budget constraints recorded: local models only, no paid keys; Sarvam vision capped at 54 calls; 1800 total calls (18x100); cost-tracking report required at validation call.
benchmark-optimization-loop (variant search per language) rejected because probe22 GT verdicts locked; Skill-comply/automation-audit-ops UNKNOWN, only if evidence of need.
AdaptOrch per-language topology proposal: weak cells (Santali, Kashmiri, OldScan) hierarchical/more supervision; Odia parallel; routing from probe22 CER baseline. Speculative; not measured.
Verdict dual verification (santa-method): two independent passes e.g. CER + visual inspection or two different CER scorers; both must pass.

Agent SDK facts (docs dated 2026-09-27): Python/TS SDK, AgentDefinition fields, hooks (command/http/mcp_tool/prompt/subagent), SubagentHandback v2.1.271+, skills discovery. Generic tooling; no OCR evidence.
Kimi K2 (1T/32B active), K3 (2.8T params, 1M ctx, open weights) judged DIES for offline: too large / needs paid API key; Kimi K2/K3 listed as UNKNOWN for weak-cell validation, no OCR evidence.

Laya (NandhaKishorM) non-autoregressive System-1 router ~33ms, 100+ langs, detect_script, ece_score: candidate for script routing / confidence gating; unmeasured on OCR. Layla is a different project. ScopeGate: capability gating != per-call authorization.

MCP registry/OAuth 2.1, Obsidian agent plugins, OpenCode skills/ECC agents (26 agents/26 cmds vs variant 12 agents/31 cmds), Vercel AI SDK/LangChain.js/Cursor SDK: generic tooling docs with no OCR content; Cursor SDK DIES (paid key).

Plan v4 does not carry the 'fix-loop max 2 rounds' + independent Verdict + human validation-call discipline or the evidence-status law (PRIMARY/MEASURED/DERIVED...) from the campaign (artifact_230:96, artifact_220:82).

Weak-cell thresholds (Santali>55, Kashmiri>55, OldScan>55, Odia>80) and baselines (Santali 53.91, Kashmiri 54.82, OldScan 55.3, Odia 80.01) from the 18x100 probe are absent from Plan v4 (artifact_200:12, artifact_260:54).
Plan v4 should state budget/cost caps if any API experts are used (Sarvam 54-call cap, 1800-call lock; artifact_270:124) and the no-paid-key constraint's effect on Gemini/Sarvam comparators.
